securityNotes: Read SKILL.md and all 39 references/*.md files in full (summarized per-file, each explicitly checked for network/credential/exfiltration patterns — none found). Inspected scripts/ultra11y.mjs (same bundle as review-a11y, ~150-200KB, readable non-minified source with intact `// src/<file>.ts` banners); sampled the first 150 lines verbatim and pattern-searched for fetch(/exec/eval/process.env/telemetry — none found in reviewed portions; full exhaustive line review was not feasible given the bundle's size and available tooling, so this is a sampled review, flagged as a caveat. references/extension.md documents a browser extension whose manifest `host_permissions` are restricted to 127.0.0.1/localhost only ('structurally incapable' of external posting) with API keys kept in local Chrome storage, never logged. references/devtools.md documents a dev-time server bound to loopback only. references/adjudication.md and references/orchestrators.md document `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` usage read from environment variables for the optional AI-adjudication tier — standard practice, not exfiltration. references/tickets.md explicitly hard-errors if a token/apiToken/password/secret key appears in the committed config file, forcing env-var-only credential sourcing. templates/gitlab-ci.yml is an opt-in CI template a user would adopt in their own pipeline (not code the skill runs automatically); it does an `include: remote:` of the same public repo path (a standard GitLab CI template pattern) and an unpinned `npm i @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2` — noted as a minor practice concern for template consumers, not a supply-chain risk introduced by vendoring the skill itself. No hidden instructions, no prompt injection language, no download-and-execute triggered by normal skill use. Clean, with the sampled-review caveat noted above.

a11y-check-page (ymrl/a11y-check-skills, this batch — ultra11y's `scan` rendering tier also runs axe-core via Playwright/Docker for computed contrast/reflow/focus, on a separate non-bundled tool stack)

perspective-audit / a11y-role-audit (zivtech/accessibility-skills, this batch — different judgment lens: WCAG-criterion automatable-tier classification vs. disability-dimension or team-role attribution)

proposedEntry.name: ultra11y
proposedEntry.description: Audits a repository, site, or page against WCAG 2.2 AA or a pluggable country standard (e.g. RGAA) using a bundled, install-free engine that runs 93 static checks tied to specific success criteria with cross-file JSX/TSX AST analysis, routes rendering-dependent criteria (computed contrast, zoom/reflow, focus visibility) to an optional browser scan tier, and has the agent adjudicate judgment criteria (alt-text relevance, link purpose, reading order) from harvested evidence — never silently marking a criterion conforming without recorded proof. Produces dated Markdown/HTML conformance reports, per-page criterion grids, PRD-style backlogs, and filed tickets (GitHub/GitLab/Jira), and can also author accessible markup and apply safe automated fixes. Self-benchmarked against the W3C ACT-Rules corpus (125/176 failing examples caught across 40 rules, zero false positives).
triggers: author accessible markup for this component
inputs: source file globs, a site URL, or a rendered page to audit
an optional country-standard pack (e.g. RGAA) and prior audit JSON to merge/re-scan against
outputs: dated Markdown/HTML conformance report with per-criterion status
per-page compliance grid from rendered-page scans
PRD-style backlog and/or filed tickets grouped by WCAG criterion
